routes.label: Combine the rate and time ratios

question: Josh and Mike live \(13\) miles apart. Yesterday Josh started to ride his bicycle toward Mike’s house. A little later Mike started to ride his bicycle toward Josh’s house. When they met, Josh had ridden for twice the length of time as Mike and at four-fifths of Mike’s rate. How many miles had Mike ridden when they met?
solution:
Distance equals rate times time, so both the rate comparison and the riding-time comparison affect the distances. Josh rides at \(\frac45\) of Mike’s rate for twice as long. His distance is therefore
\[
\frac45\cdot2=\frac85
\]
of Mike’s distance. Thus Josh’s and Mike’s distances are in the ratio \(8:5\).

Because they ride toward each other and meet between their houses, their distances add to \(13\) miles. The ratio has \(8+5=13\) equal parts, so each part represents \(1\) mile. Mike’s five parts give \(\boxed{5\text{ miles}}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
